body.x: This is "Weekly Gwangju AI" to look into the news and issues that drew attention in Gwangju. The reporting team from Aving News recently met with InDJ, a Gwangju-based company that provides a music recommendation service using AI technology to analyze situations and emotions.

The company won the innovation award at CES 2023, making it the only Gwangju-based company to receive the award. InDJ CEO Jung Woo-ju said in an interview that the company is playing a role in mining future gold and will enter the global market. The future of InDJ, which Gwangju is paying attention to, is worth watching.

Recently, Honam University introduced the AI Cube Academy through its Honam University YouTube channel. It is a course developed to enhance students' capabilities and introduce new technology trends such as AI and metaverse to citizens.

Leading experts in research and education participated as instructors. Baek Lan, Honam University Professor and Director of the AI Convergence College, said that the AI Cube Academy course is available for free to foster the digital competence of all citizens and expects much attention. The course can be viewed through Honam University TV.

On the 26th, Gwangju Creative Economy Innovation Center held the Gwangju Startup Forum at the Kim Dae-jung Convention Center, which was attended by prospective startup entrepreneurs, startups, and investors. Officials from startup support agencies explained government support programs. Kim Jin-hyung, a KAIST professor, gave a lecture on "ChatGPT."

An investment briefing was also held, with companies such as Share plat, The InTech, and SafeMotion participating. They emphasized their company's introduction and vision. Safe Motion's Oh Chi-min introduced a behavior recognition program, which is expected to receive significant interest in the market.

The Aving News reporting team also met recently with Kim Min-seok, the CEO of Boot Camp, a company developing services for the health management of seniors. The company uses smartphone sensors to check health conditions and prevent fall accidents. Kim Min-seok said, "This year will be a year to confirm Boot Camp's potential."

The Aving News reporting team also met with Jung Sung-hoon, CEO of Unmanned Systems, a company developing a system that can autonomously acquire spatial information. The company is also developing unmanned aerial vehicles and underwater drones. Jung Sung-hoon said, "We are developing technology for full automation and aiming to provide the collected data inexpensively."
We will continue to provide a summary of the major news.
△ Kim Young-jip, the director of Gwangju Techno Park, returned from a business trip to Japan where he made progress in investment attraction and AI industry cooperation.
△ Kim Joon-ha, the head of the AI Industry Cluster Agency, conducted the third ChatGPT education session for Gwangju citizens, which received a positive response.

△ The Jeonnam Information and Culture Industry Promotion Agency is supporting content companies. The target is a company that produces webtoons, video contents, and contents using local specialized resources.

△ The AI Industry Cluster Agency is recruiting AI companies in Gwangju for participation in the AI Data Voucher support program, which supports energy, automotive, healthcare, and cultural content sectors.
△ The National Science Museum in Gwangju will hold a "Science Night Festival" on the 29th, targeting adults as the audience.

That was ‘Weekly Gwangju AI.’ An AI announcer has delivered Gwangju’s AI news. The manuscript was written with the help of Chat GPT. The news is reported through platforms such as Naver, Daum, Google, and others worldwide. You can inquire about the promotion by e-mail.
